description:
A QA engineer has identified that the permissions on the test environment's private SSH key file, located at /home/user/test-environment/id_rsa, are too open and cause SSH clients to warn: "Permissions 0644 for '/home/user/test-environment/id_rsa' are too open." To secure the environment and ensure SSH will use this key, restrict the file's permissions so that only the file's owner can read and write it. After adjusting the permissions, generate a verification log at /home/user/fix_permissions.log that contains exactly one line in the following format: 
id_rsa permissions: [PERMS]
where [PERMS] is the four-digit octal permission of /home/user/test-environment/id_rsa (e.g., 0600), without quotes or extra whitespace. The log file must match the above format and must not include additional lines, headers, or console output.
truth:
Before the task begins, the file /home/user/test-environment/id_rsa exists with permissions set to 0644 and is owned by user "user". 

After the task, /home/user/test-environment/id_rsa must exist and have permissions set to 0600. Ownership should remain unchanged (user:user).

A new file /home/user/fix_permissions.log must be created with the following single line (and no trailing whitespace):

id_rsa permissions: 0600

If /home/user/fix_permissions.log exists, it must be overwritten with the updated content above.
